hints: Apply the factor and remainder theorems: divisibility by $2x-1$ gives $p(\tfrac12)=0$, while the remainder on division by $x+2$ gives $p(-2)=5$.
Substitute each input into $p(x)=ax^3+x^2+bx+3$ and simplify to two linear equations in $a$ and $b$.
Solve those simultaneous equations and check both original polynomial conditions.
walkthrough:
Apply the Factor Theorem: since $p(x) = ax^3 + x^2 + bx + 3$ is divisible by $(2x - 1)$, we have $p\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$:
$$a\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + b\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 3 = 0$$
$$\dfrac{1}{8}a + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}b + 3 = 0$$

Multiply the equation by $8$ to eliminate the denominators and simplify:
$$a + 2 + 4b + 24 = 0$$
$$a + 4b + 26 = 0 \implies a + 4b = -26 \quad [\text{Equation 1}]$$

Apply the Remainder Theorem: when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x + 2)$, the remainder is $5$, so $p(-2) = 5$:
$$a(-2)^3 + (-2)^2 + b(-2) + 3 = 5$$
$$-8a + 4 - 2b + 3 = 5$$
$$-8a - 2b + 7 = 5$$
$$-8a - 2b = -2$$

Solve the simultaneous equations by expressing $b$ from [Equation 2]:
$$b = 1 - 4a$$
Substitute $b = 1 - 4a$ into [Equation 1]:
$$a + 4(1 - 4a) = -26$$
$$a + 4 - 16a = -26$$
$$-15a + 4 = -26$$
$$-15a = -30 \implies a = 2$$

State the values of $a$ and $b$:
$$a = 2, \quad b = -7$$
